Did you know that you already have a built-in tool for screen recording on your Windows laptop? Today, I’ll show you how to screen record effortlessly using the Snipping Tool that's already installed. No extra software required!

In this video, you'll learn how to:
- Use the Windows shortcut (Windows + Shift + R) to open the Snipping Tool.
- Select specific areas or the entire screen for recording.
- Turn your microphone on/off and record system audio.
- Start, pause, and stop your recording.
- Save your screen recordings as an MP4.
- Edit your recordings using Clipchamp, a free video editor from Microsoft.

The Snipping Tool is surprisingly powerful for screen recording, and I'll walk you through all the key features you need to get started. Give it a try and let me know in the comments if you found this helpful!

In this tutorial you'll learn how to make a cinematic product commercial entirely with AI — no camera, no crew, no studio. We build every asset from scratch in Soul Cinema and GPT Image 2.0, use a custom Claude skill to turn a script into a connected shotlist of Seedance 2.0 prompts, then generate and iterate every scene — all inside Higgsfield AI. Google just replaced its most popular photo editor — and every image it makes carries a secret mark you can't see. Nano Banana 2.1 (released October 6, 2026) edits any photo with a single sentence: outfit swaps, background changes, merging two photos into one, product mockups, even legible text inside images — all in about ten seconds. This tutorial runs five killer demos, then reveals the three catches Google buried in the fine print: the invisible watermark on every image, the paywall locking out free users, and the "half price" headline hiding tripled input costs.

0:00 Google replaced its photo editor (the secret mark)
0:45 What Nano Banana 2.1 actually is
1:40 Demo 1 — outfit swap
2:28 Demo 2 — background swap
3:15 Demo 3 — merging two photos

videos.title: Spin faster by going smaller! 🌀 #DrTatiana #science #funny #shorts
videos.description:
You can try this demonstration yourself using a spinning stool (or office chair) and two small weights to explore the power of conservation of angular momentum. You start by spinning slowly with arms stretched out to the sides. But when the weights are pulled close to the body, the spinning suddenly speeds up.

This happens because, when no outside torques are acting, an object’s angular momentum stays the same. But the angular momentum is a product of the rotational velocity and rotational inertia which is basically how the weight is spread out. Changing it—arms wide versus arms close—affects how fast the body spins. Pulling the arms in makes you spin faster to conserve angular momentum. It’s the same principle figure skaters use when they pull their arms in to spin faster. To feel it, you need to be on ice, or on a rotating stool with low friction, or floating in space!

This was presented by Dr. Tatiana Erukhimova, professor at Texas A&M University @tamu.

videos.title: ZAP!  #science #animation #funny #learn #explainer
videos.description:
Fluffy socks + fluffy rug = Max is now a walking hazard. ⚡😱

Why do you get zapped touching a door handle? Ribbit explains: when your socks rub on a rug, tiny bits of charge hop across and build up all over you. Touch metal, and it all jumps across in one tiny spark. ZAP! A shock you can feel is thousands of volts, but it’s over in a flash, so it can’t hurt you. (It can hurt your feelings, says Max.)

It’s worse in dry winter air, because damp air quietly leaks the charge away. Highveld winters, we’re looking at you. 🥶

Tip: touch metal with a key first, and the spark jumps to the key instead of your fingertip. 🔑

Tiger did not enjoy his part of the experiment. 🐱⚡

What’s the worst thing that’s ever ZAPPED you? Tell us in the comments 👇

🔔 Follow for more weird everyday science with Ribbit, Max, Lily and Tiger!

Sources: SciShow, “How to Stop Getting Zapped by Static”; Discovery, “Here’s Why Static Shock Is Worse in Winter”

#shorts #science #funfacts #staticelectricity #howdoesthatwork #ribbit #animation #physics

videos.title: WHO FARTED?! #science #animation #funny #explainer #learn
videos.description:
Someone on this deck did it, and Max is going to find out who. 🕵️💨

Biscuit is suspect one. Flat-faced dogs gulp lots of air, and it has to come out, but swallowed air has no smell. Free the dog. 🐶

Ribbit explains: nearly all of a fart smells of nothing. The stink is under one percent, mostly sulfur gases made by the bacteria in your gut as they munch your leftovers. You have trillions of them. Max did not take this well. 🦠

Eggs, meat, onions and garlic can make it worse. One small study found women’s farts smelled stronger, and in one huge study, people admitted to about five a day. Admitted. 🥚

Tiger didn’t survive the investigation. Neither did Max’s dignity. 🐱

There’s a clue in the very first second. Who REALLY did it? Tell us in the comments 👇

🔔 Follow for more weird everyday science with Ribbit, Max, Lily and Tiger!

Sources: Suarez et al., Gut, 1998; Brindal et al., JAMA Network Open, 2026; Sender et al., PLOS Biology, 2016

#shorts #science #funfacts #farts #howdoesthatwork #ribbit #animation #whodunnit

videos.title: ALMOST GOT HIM!  #science #animation #funny #explainer
videos.description:
Mosquito 12. Everyone else 0. 🦟😎

Max has slapped himself nine times trying to get one mosquito, and it turns out his hand is helping it escape. Ribbit explains: a moving hand pushes a wave of air ahead of it. The mosquito makes a sharp turn, then rides that wave to safety. It’s basically surfing your hand. 🏄

Scientists tested this with high-speed cameras, filming almost 500 mosquito escapes. It’s also why fly swatters have holes: the air slips through, so there’s less wave to ride.

Not that a swatter helped Max. Or Ribbit’s tongue. 👅

What’s the worst thing YOU’VE hit trying to get a mosquito? Tell us in the comments 👇

🔔 Follow for more weird everyday science with Ribbit, Max, Lily and Tiger!

Source: Cribellier, Camilo, Goyal & Muijres, Current Biology, 2024 (Wageningen University)

Zookeepers Break Concrete to Save Trapped Giraffe
videos.description:
A Little Wisdom Helps You Become Smarter !

In the video, zoo staff are performing an urgent rescue of a giraffe with its head trapped in an artificial tree root structure made of concrete. The giraffe is lying on its side, against the metal fence of its enclosure. The decorative rock and root formations, while visually natural, have created a dangerous gap. A rescuer is carefully using a hammer to break the hard concrete to free the animal's head. This incident highlights a significant hazard in habitat design. Such man-made structures, though aesthetically pleasing, can pose unforeseen risks to large, curious animals. To prevent this, enclosures must be carefully inspected for any gaps that could trap an animal's head or limbs. All decorative elements should be tested for safety with the specific animal species in mind. Using softer, more flexible materials for complex shapes can greatly enhance safety. Regular safety reviews of all habitat features are essential. This event serves as a critical lesson in prioritizing animal welfare over pure visual design. The primary goal of any enclosure must be to provide a secure and hazard-free environment for its inhabitants.

videos.title: Brave Cat Battles Fox, Saves Chicken in Farmyard Showdown. Epic Animal Rescue Caught on Camera
videos.description:
Feb 13, 2026

From a Jen Merriman video, a quiet farmyard on a seemingly ordinary day suddenly turn into a pulse pounding showdown when a sly fox decides it wants dinner, and that dinner happens to be a white chicken. The chicken flaps and squawks, trying to escape the fox’s jaws, but the predator is fast and determined. Just when it seems like all hope is lost, a fearless tabby cat bursts onto the scene. 

With the speed and precision of a seasoned hunter, the cat charges at the fox, claws ready and eyes locked on the target. In an instant, chaos erupts: the cat leaps onto the fox’s back, forcing it to stumble, feathers fly everywhere, and the chicken tumbles to the ground, free at last. The fox, thoroughly outmatched and embarrassed, scrambles into the bushes with tail tucked, leaving the cat standing victorious. 

Meanwhile, the chicken shakes off its ruffled feathers and struts away like nothing happened, clearly grateful but also slightly bewildered by its dramatic rescue. The cat, having completed its daring mission, strolls through the farmyard, utterly unfazed by the chaos it just stopped. This short but epic encounter shows the bravery and quick thinking of domestic cats, proving that even the smallest heroes can turn the tide in surprising ways. Farm life is never dull, and courage often comes in furry packages.

The secret formula behind Johnny Harris' popular explainer videos. A visual look at how this ex Vox "Borders" video maker structures his journalism, map, & historical stories. Insight into scripting & editing YouTube videos that inspire, retain viewers, & get views.

The clips of Johnny Harris explaining his structure come from a much larger talk he gave, I've linked to the region I sampled from here:
https://youtu.be/lRq6rIiGFAU?t=3301

Those ideas were used as a base, but much of the ideas were original, for example, the "experience it, understand it", which my creative editor Michelle Jia helped come up with.

It's also important to note:
1. This structure isn't Johnny's creation: he learned it in large part at Vox under the mentorship of folks like Joss Fong.
2. Beyond his structure, Johnny Harris puts weeks of effort into deeply understanding a topic, which enables him to use this story structure so effectively. It's not the structure alone doing all the work :)

Rivers become curvier and curvier until they bump into themselves. Then, lakes follow the route of least resistance and connect to form a straighter route. What’s left over is called an Oxbow lake… but they go by a lot of different names. 

In Australia they are referred to as Billabongs; in South Texas, they are called resacas, sometimes they are called ‘horseshoe lakes’.

videos.title: Why Do Time Zones Look So Strange 🌍 How They Work 🕒
videos.description:
Why do time zones look so weird?! 🌍 You probably know that the Earth is divided into 24 time zones, but have you ever wondered why they look so strange? 🤔 Dive into the fascinating world of time zones, starting at the prime meridian in Greenwich, 0 UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). Discover why time zones east of Greenwich have positive offsets and those to the west have negative offsets. 🌐 Explore the practical reasons behind the irregular boundaries of time zones. Imagine if time zones were perfectly straight lines - cities like Chicago would be split between different time zones, causing major confusion! 🏙️ Learn how political, economic, and social factors influence the layout of time zones and why countries like France have the most time zones due to their overseas territories, while China, despite spanning five time zones, uses just one. 🇫🇷🇨🇳 Uncover why places like Kashgar in western China experience darkness even at 10 AM. 🌅 Don't miss this intriguing look at the world of time zones! 📅🕒

videos.title: The Difference Between UAE, Dubai & Abu Dhabi 🇦🇪 What Are the Emirates 🤯
videos.description:
Many people don’t know the difference between the UAE, Abu Dhabi, and Dubai 🇦🇪 The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is a country in the Middle East, located on the eastern part of the Arabian Peninsula. It covers about 83,000 square km, comparable in size to Portugal or Austria. The UAE is a federation made up of 7 emirates, similar to U.S. states, except here they’re called emirates, which is where the country gets its name. Each emirate is ruled by a sheikh and power stays within the ruling family, essentially functioning as a monarchy 👑 All 7 rulers form the Federal Supreme Council and elect the President of the UAE. By tradition, the president is the ruler of Abu Dhabi - the largest emirate, covering about 85% of the UAE’s territory. Abu Dhabi also includes Abu Dhabi City, the UAE’s capital and the seat of the federal government 🏛️ Dubai, is a different emirate with a city of the same name. Dubai became world-famous for its luxury lifestyle, the world’s tallest skyscraper, Burj Khalifa, the massive Dubai Mall 🛍️, and palm-shaped artificial islands 🌴 filled with resorts, hotels and villas 🌊

videos.title: 🌪️ Hurricanes, Tornadoes, Typhoons, Cyclones & Monsoons 🌧️ What’s the Difference?
videos.description:
🌪️ You've probably heard of hurricanes, tornadoes, typhoons, cyclones, and monsoons, but do you know the differences between them? 🌊 Let's break it down! Hurricanes, typhoons, and cyclones are actually the same phenomenon—massive tropical storms that form over water. The only difference is where they form: hurricanes in the Atlantic and northeastern Pacific, typhoons in the northwestern Pacific, and cyclones in the South Pacific and Indian Ocean. Interestingly, cyclones rotate in the opposite direction because they form in the Southern Hemisphere. Tornadoes, on the other hand, are smaller but incredibly powerful rotating columns of air that form only over land, with the United States being a hotspot. 🌪️ And then there are monsoons—seasonal winds that bring heavy rains, especially in South Asia, where they play a crucial role in shaping the climate and agriculture. 🌧️

Many people get confused about the difference between New York, New York City, Manhattan and Long Island. 🗽 New York is one of the 50 U.S. states, divided into 62 counties and five of them are unique because together they form New York City 🌆 NYC is the largest city in the state, even though the capital is surprisingly Albany and about 8.5 million people live here, nearly half of the state’s population. videos.title: All Maps are Lying to You 😱 The Real Size of Counties 🗺️
videos.description:
Did you know that all maps are lying to you? 🗺️ Uncover the truth behind the distortion that lurks within every map. The map we often rely on in our daily lives, known as the Mercator projection, serves us well for navigation 🧭 but comes with a significant flaw: it distorts the sizes and proportions of landmasses. Take, for instance, the colossal Greenland and compare it to the vast expanse of Africa. 🌍 On our maps, they appear to be nearly the same size, but in reality, Greenland is several times smaller than Africa. This distortion arises from the challenge of representing the curved surface of our spherical planet on a flat map, a process known as projection. Various types of projections exist, each introducing its own set of distortions or inconveniences. The Mercator projection, favored for its navigational utility, preserves shape but sacrifices accurate proportions. A visual demonstration of what the world truly looks like when portrayed with correct proportions. Countries closer to the equator maintain their accurate sizes and shapes, while those farther away stretch unnaturally upward, exaggerating their scale. 📏

videos.title: Why there are 2 Irelands 🇮🇪🇬🇧 Ireland vs Northern Ireland 🤯
videos.description:
Why does Ireland have TWO countries on one island? 🇮🇪🇬🇧 It looks simple on the map… but this border is the result of centuries of invasions, settlements and conflict. First came the Celts, shaping the island’s language and culture. Then the Vikings arrived, not just to raid, but to stay, founding key cities across Ireland. Later, the island was divided into multiple kingdoms that fought each other more than they united. Everything changed when the English were invited to help… and decided not to leave. Over time, they took control of the entire island, but constant Irish rebellions made that control unstable. So Britain made a strategic move: settling loyal Protestant populations in the north, giving them land, power and privileges. This created a deep division. After the Irish War of Independence, the island was divided. Ireland became independent 🇮🇪 Northern Ireland remained part of the United Kingdom 🇬🇧

videos.title: All Maps Lie! The Mercator Projection, The Most Commonly Looked at Map In The World, isn't So Right.
videos.description:
From original on TikTok @map_nerd:

There’s a basic problem in showing the world on a flat map. The world's not flat, so that’s the problem. 

When you take something that’s a round globe and try to flatten it out, things get very distorted; like a lot of places that look tiny are much bigger, and places that look massive are actually tiny. 

Australia is actually a similar size to the lower 48 of the US even tho it looks like a much smaller island. Brazil is actually bigger than the contiguous US. (Contiguous= not counting Alaska, Hawaii). The whole of The UK (Britain) fits into Michigan. 

And that giant thing on the top of every map that towers over everything - Greenland - its really not that big - it’s more like the size of Mexico. 

Maps you look at everyday , like Google Maps and the ones you pull down in school (do they still have those?) don’t actually show the world as it really is. They can’t. 

It’s actually physically impossible to flatten a sphere without distorting it somehow. Try it.

The most commonly used map type - called the Mercator Projection - was designed over 450 years ago and it was made that way mainly so boats could navigate without getting totally confused. Now it’s pretty much ingrained in everything we look at. There’s lots of debate if it’s the best way to look at the world for a lot of reasons (including the fact that it seems to favor places like Europe at the expense of places like Africa). 

There’s lots of other ways to make a flat map of the world but none will ever be perfect. check them out - it might change how you look at the world.

videos.title: How Does Brazil Vote?
videos.description:
Brazil's 2026 runoff split almost exactly in half: Lula 51.8%, Flávio Bolsonaro 48.2%. But the map behind that split is newer than it looks. In 1998, Lula carried just two states and almost all of the Northeast voted for the government. This animated explainer follows how Bolsa Família, the 2005 scandal and the 2006 election flipped the map, why the South and the farm frontier vote right, why the Northeast votes for Lula, and why Minas Gerais keeps picking the winner.

videos.title: What Is El Niño & Why Is It So Powerful 🌡️🤯 Super El Niño 🌊
videos.description:
What causes El Niño and how does it affect weather around the world? 🌊 The 2026 super El Niño could become one of the strongest on record, bringing warmer winters to Canada, heavier rain to the southern United States and flooding to parts of South America, while Australia and Indonesia face drought 🌎 It starts in the Pacific Ocean, where trade winds normally push warm surface water toward Indonesia and northern Australia. Cold water off Peru and southern Ecuador helps keep the coast dry. Every two to seven years, these winds weaken and warm water spreads east. Sea surface temperatures just 1–2°C above normal can shift global weather patterns. In the 1870s, a powerful El Niño contributed to a famine that took millions of lives 🌡️ Forecasts suggest this super El Niño could push temperatures in parts of the eastern Pacific more than 3°C above normal. As the ocean releases heat into the atmosphere, global temperatures rise and 2027 could become the hottest year ever recorded.

videos.title: Nepal Floods 2026 Explained: What Caused the Deadly Flash Flood?
videos.description:
What caused the catastrophic Nepal floods of August 2026?

At 08:37 on the 26th of August 2026, a mountain on the border between Nepal and Tibet came apart. Seven and a half hours later, the water it made was still moving — 168 kilometres downstream.

This is how that happened, in order, and why most of what was published in the first twenty-four hours was wrong. It was not an earthquake, though seismometers recorded it as one. It was not a glacial lake outburst, though that is normally the right answer.

Throughout, three labels: ESTABLISHED, DISPUTED, UNKNOWN. Where the science is unfinished, I say so rather than smoothing it over.

CHAPTERS

6:17  Bulking: why the flood grew six times

videos.title: Nepal Flood Disaster 2026: Glacier Collapse
videos.description: Nepal-Tibet border glacier disaster is in news after a huge ice-rock avalanche triggered a destructive flash flood on 26 August 2026 near the Rasuwagadhi-Gyirong border corridor. For UPSC 2027 and UPSC Prelims, this topic is important for Geography, Environment, disaster management, Himalayan hazards, glacial collapse, GLOF-like events, early warning and climate risk. Reports say the lower part of a glacier broke off at high altitude, fell about 1,200 metres and entered the Lhende Khola. Debris may have briefly blocked the river before releasing a fast surge of water, mud, ice, rocks and boulders into the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli systems. The flood damaged roads, bridges, hydropower sites, gauges, power lines and communications, while casualty and missing-person numbers continued to change. The case shows how a collapse high in the Himalayas can become a downstream disaster within minutes. It highlights the need for glacier monitoring, hazard mapping, resilient roads and transboundary early-warning systems. Watch more UPSC current affairs explainers on Clarity UPSC.

videos.description:
This video is about "AMUL 🐄 The Revolution That Saved Millions of Farmers | Case Study | White Revolution | Live Hindi"

In this in-depth video, we explore the Amul success story, a tale of innovation, resilience, and empowerment that revolutionized India’s dairy industry and transformed it into the world’s largest milk producer. This is the inspiring journey of Dr. Verghese Kurien, hailed as the Father of the White Revolution, and Tribhuvandas Patel, who laid the foundation for Amul's cooperative model to uplift the Farmers of Gujarat.

How It All Began
Amul’s story began in 1946 when farmers in Gujarat were exploited by middlemen and faced unfair practices. Tribhuvandas Patel, a visionary leader, united these farmers to establish a cooperative, creating the Kaira District Cooperative Milk Producers Union Ltd., famously known as Amul. But the journey wasn’t easy. In 1949, Dr. Verghese Kurien, an engineering graduate, joined the cooperative and introduced groundbreaking ideas to revolutionize the dairy sector. Together, Patel and Kurien empowered 36 lakh farmers, providing them with a sustainable livelihood and hope for a better future.

The White Revolution and Operation Flood
Dr. Kurien spearheaded Operation Flood, the largest dairy development program in the world. This initiative not only made India self-sufficient in milk production but also turned it into the largest producer globally. This video sheds light on How Amul Saved India from milk shortages and laid the foundation for rural development, women’s empowerment, and economic independence.

Marketing Genius and the Amul Girl
Amul’s success is not just about milk; it’s also about branding. The genius of Sylvester daCunha, the creator of the iconic Amul Girl, brought a fresh and witty perspective to advertising. These advertisements became a cultural phenomenon, resonating with every Indian household and ensuring Amul’s dominance in the market.

How Amul Killed Competition
Through innovation, fair pricing, and a farmer-first approach, Amul outperformed its competitors, many of whom were multinational giants. This AMUL Case Study demonstrates how the cooperative model can thrive in a competitive landscape, ensuring quality products while supporting its backbone—the farmers.

The Untold Story of White Revolution

videos.title: How Minimalist Conquered India's D2C Beauty Market? - Business Case Study
videos.description:
00:00 - Intro
01:09 - Early Days
02:54 - Origin of Minimalist
05:35 - Crazy Growth
08:21 - Financials: breaking down profitability
11:10 - 3,000 Crore Exit and Road Ahead

HUL’s recent ₹3,000 crore acquisition of Minimalist marks India's biggest all-cash D2C deal. Founded in 2020 in Jaipur, this young brand managed to disrupt a competitive beauty industry dominated by giants like HUL and Unilever. What makes this deal extraordinary is that the founders, Rahul and Mohit Yadav, retained 60% equity, earning ₹1,700 crore in cash.

Founding & Early Days
Before Minimalist, the Yadav brothers had launched Freewill in 2018, a personalized haircare brand. Despite positive customer response, it failed to scale due to high costs and complexity. This experience made them realize that India’s beauty industry relied heavily on marketing rather than effective products.

The Birth of Minimalist
Inspired by The Ordinary, a Canadian skincare brand known for transparency, the Yadavs launched Minimalist in 2020. Unlike brands exploiting the “organic” and “natural” narrative, Minimalist openly displayed ingredients, emphasizing that not all chemicals are harmful.

With just 1,000 face serum bottles and no marketing budget, Minimalist tested the waters via an Instagram post. Beauty influencers organically discovered and promoted it, leading to rapid traction. Some accused them of copying The Ordinary, but the founders openly acknowledged their inspiration.

Growth Strategy
Instead of pouring money into influencer marketing like competitors such as Mamaearth, Minimalist relied on genuine customer testimonials, making their brand appear more authentic. Their marketing spend was only 25% of revenue (vs. 40–50% for others), while their customer repeat rate stood at 60%—three times the industry average.

This efficiency helped Minimalist reach ₹100 crore in revenue in just eight months, a milestone that took Mamaearth three years to achieve. The brand’s lean product catalog also ensured better inventory control and operational efficiency.

Financials & Profitability Challenges
Despite rising revenue, Minimalist’s profit margins dropped from 20% to 3% (FY21–FY24) due to high manufacturing costs. Unlike others, Minimalist owned its production facilities, prioritizing quality over cost-cutting. Their Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) was 35%, higher than industry standards (Mamaearth at 30%).

Minimalist’s strategy mirrored Tesla’s: invest in superior products and let customer satisfaction drive marketing.

Online-First Strategy & Offline Expansion
Initially, Minimalist focused on online sales, ensuring that customers understood the science behind skincare. However, scaling beyond ₹500 crore required offline expansion. HUL’s acquisition gives Minimalist access to its vast retail network of 9 million stores, enabling broader distribution.

HUL’s Acquisition & The Ordinary’s Entry
Minimalist’s biggest challenge is The Ordinary’s entry into India via Nykaa, backed by Estée Lauder. To compete, Minimalist needed HUL’s financial and distribution strength. This acquisition ensures Minimalist remains a leader in India’s science-backed skincare market.

The Big Question
With HUL’s support, can Minimalist continue to dominate the Indian market, or will The Ordinary take over?

In FY-2023, India's logistics costs exceeded 14% of its GDP, significantly higher than China's 10%. This highlights the inefficiency and high expenses of India's supply chain compared to more efficient nations like Vietnam and Thailand. The Indian government has acknowledged this issue, launching a national logistics policy in 2022 aiming to reduce these costs to 8%, aligning with developed countries. However, government policies alone are insufficient; the private sector and startups must also contribute to addressing these inefficiencies.

One such startup, Porter, has emerged as a rapidly growing logistics company in India. Inspired by Uber's transformation of the taxi industry, Porter aims to revolutionize last-mile logistics in India, targeting a $200 billion market. To understand Porter's impact, it is essential to comprehend the problem it addresses: intracity logistics, which involves transporting goods within a city. Efficient logistics are crucial for economic productivity, and in India, 90% of the sector remains unorganized.

Porter was founded by Uttam Digga and Pranav Goel, two IIT Kharagpur alumni who identified the inefficiencies in the logistics sector, similar to those in the pre-Uber taxi industry. Small business owners faced challenges such as difficulty finding drivers, high costs, and unreliable delivery times. Inspired by Uber's success, Digga and Goel sought to create a marketplace connecting truck drivers with customers, improving vehicle utilization and reducing costs.

In 2013, while working as analysts at JP Morgan, Digga and Goel were inspired by Uber's use of technology to optimize the ride-hailing industry. They noticed numerous light commercial vehicles parked unused and realized the potential for a similar solution in logistics. They spoke with over 500 truck drivers and discovered the inefficiencies in their industry, with drivers averaging only 1-2 orders per day despite the capacity for 4-5. This led to the birth of Porter, aiming to replicate Uber's model for goods transportation.

Initially, Porter operated manually with Digga and Goel dividing responsibilities: Digga onboarded truck drivers, while Goel secured customers. Using just a phone and Google Sheets, they managed the operations without an app. As their customer base grew, they brought in Vikas Choudhary, a tech expert from IIT Kanpur, to develop their technology platform. By pitching their service as 20% cheaper, Porter quickly attracted over 500 business customers, processing 3,000 bookings monthly and generating significant revenue.

Porter's early success enabled them to raise $500,000 in seed funding and $5.5 million in a Series A round. However, growth brought challenges. In 2015, flush with funding, they prematurely expanded into intercity logistics, an already crowded market. This expansion strained their resources, leading to a temporary closure of the new vertical and layoffs. Additionally, their initial pricing strategy became less effective, necessitating a focus on improving service quality.

To enhance customer experience, Porter ensured timely driver arrivals and deliveries. They leveraged their app to track drivers via GPS, providing real-time updates to customers and reallocating drivers in case of delays. They also addressed inefficiencies at loading and unloading stations by introducing per-minute charges, and incentivizing punctuality among customers.

These improvements led to significant growth, with Porter ensuring that 80% of their drivers received return trip orders, increasing their earnings by 20-30%. This efficiency attracted attention, resulting in Mahindra Group merging their logistics platform, SmartShift, with Porter and investing $10 million.

videos.title: Inside Major Corporate Accounting Scandals | Bigger Than Enron (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
videos.description:
Enron’s spectacular collapse in the early 2000s was at the time the biggest financial scandal in U.S. history. It didn’t happen in a vacuum — and it revealed systemic problems far beyond a single company. (Aired 2002)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

In the 2002 documentary “Bigger Than Enron,” Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Hedrick Smith looked at Enron’s implosion and asked, “Where were the watchdogs who were supposed to warn us when companies were playing fast and loose with their books — the stock analysts, lawyers, bankers, Securities and Exchange Commission? Above all, where were the accountants?”

“Bigger Than Enron” investigated those questions in detail, offering an in-depth look at where the U.S. financial regulation landscape stood in June 2002 after Enron’s collapse. 
The documentary is now streaming on YouTube for the first time as part of an effort to make FRONTLINE’s multi-decade reporting archive widely accessible.  

In the film, experts told Smith that what happened at Enron — a cozy collaboration between the company and its accounting firm, Arthur Andersen, that enabled Enron to overstate its profits — was far from anomalous. Smith reported that in what was described as the “go-go ‘90s,” the drive for profits was in full swing, and big accounting firms regularly worked hand-in-glove with clients and Wall Street to find loopholes in accounting rules that made companies look more successful than they really were.

“This is day-to-day business operations in accounting firms and on Wall Street,” Lynn Turner, a former Wall Street partner at an accounting firm before becoming the SEC's chief accountant, said of such practices at the time. “There is nothing extraordinary, nothing unusual in that respect, with respect to Enron.”

“Bigger Than Enron” examined three specific cases involving Andersen where misleading or fraudulent accounting practices caused enormous investor losses — at Sunbeam, Waste Management, and finally, Enron — and explored the downfall of Andersen, a firm that had previously built its reputation on rock-ribbed integrity.

The documentary also looked at how, in the decade leading up to Enron, accounting and financial industry lobbyists had successfully flexed their muscle on Capitol Hill in three battles: the fight over tort reform, the fight over stock options, and the war over a SEC attempt to rein in conflicts of interest by forcing accounting firms to separate their auditing and consulting practices.

Visit pbs.org/frontline to read about legal and regulatory developments since this documentary aired, including the Supreme Court’s 2005 overturning of Arthur Andersen’s obstruction of justice conviction.

“Bigger Than Enron” was a FRONTLINE coproduction with Hedrick Smith Productions. The writer, producer and director was Marc Shaffer. The producer and correspondent was Hedrick Smith. The executive editor of FRONTLINE was Louis Wiley Jr. The executive producer of FRONTLINE was David Fanning.

videos.description:
CHIVAYO — THE LAST FLIGHT | The Life and Death of Wicknell Chivayo

On the evening of Wednesday 30 September 2026 a helicopter carrying six people crashed in the Marondera Rural area east of Harare. The government said there were no survivors. The family confirmed that the businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife, Lucy "Lulu" Muteke, were among the dead.

This Upright Films documentary follows the boy from Chivhu who was jailed at Chikurubi, won — and was prosecuted over — the US$172 million Gwanda solar contract, was acquitted in 2023, gave away cars and buses by the dozen as "Sir Wicknell", was cleared by ZACC over the 2023 election-materials tender, and in his last year courted presidents in Kenya and Malawi and the King of Eswatini.

FAIRNESS NOTE
This film was made on the night of the crash. Details were still emerging: the names of the pilots and the two other passengers, the aircraft type and the cause had not been released. Wicknell Chivayo was convicted in 2004 and served his sentence. He was acquitted of the 2011 charges and of the Gwanda fraud charges (Harare Magistrates Court, 14 March 2023), and ZACC said in December 2025 it had found no evidence linking him to wrongdoing over the ZEC tender. videos.title: Making Elon Musk documentary brought 'almost existential fear', director says
videos.description:
Many people were too frightened to speak publicly about Elon Musk, director Alex Gibney said during the unveiling of his marathon documentary about the billionaire entrepreneur at the Venice film festival.
Subscribe ► https://www.youtube.com/user/guardianwires?sub_confirmation=1

The nearly four-hour movie charts Musk’s rise from the dotcom era to become one of the world’s most influential figures, questioning how an unelected tech titan came to wield such sway over politics and public debate.

Joined by journalist Zoë Schiffer and Ashley St Clair, Musk’s former partner and the mother of one of his children, Gibney said he began work on the project in 2023 and had originally planned a less ambitious movie.

The Tesla and SpaceX chief has dismissed the film, writing on his social media platform X this month that Gibney was biased and was «obviously going to make the most convincingly terrible hit piece on me that he can possibly think of».

Gibney, whose previous subjects have included Scientology and the collapse of the energy firm Enron, said Musk’s ascent was «the story of the confidence man» whose empire was built on an ability to sell inflated visions and hyped-up promises.

The documentary uses an AI-generated version of Musk that speaks words he has uttered over the years. Asked whether he expected legal challenges, Gibney said: «We consulted our lawyers, and they gave us a sign-off to go forward.»

For six things we learned from the Elon Musk film tap the link ► https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/state-handouts-10000-lasers-and-trumps-election-six-things-we-learned-from-the-elon-musk-film

videos.title: Backbreaking work: Deep-sea fishing in the Arctic Ocean | DW Documentary
videos.description:
A state-of-the-art fishing trawler from Cuxhaven sets sail from Tromsø to hunt for cod. The crew faces six weeks at sea, during which the men must work hard, in shifts around the clock.

The fishermen receive only a modest base salary but are paid a percentage of the sales proceeds. This means: The more they catch, the more they earn. The fishermen process the catch directly on board. But suddenly, the equipment comes to a standstill. No one knows what’s wrong. Will the crew have to return to shore?

Also on board is scientific observer Tim Schorr. His job is to document what the crew is catching from the sea. But he falls ill and must disembark as soon as possible. The problem: the nearest port is a two days’ journey away.

The film offers a glimpse into the tough business of deep-sea fishing - work the fishermen love, despite the hardships.

videos.description:

Tools I Use

I'm starting to believe most of these YouTube automation gurus have never actually run a channel. So here it is straight: how to properly start a faceless YouTube channel in 2026, including the algorithm update most people still don't understand.
Step one is your niche, and you really only have two smart options. Path one is news, because Google and YouTube's Gemini integration now rewards "net information gain" above everything else, which means a trending story beats another recycled top 10 list every time. Path two is what I call ghost niches: real topics that already exist, nobody's just covering them on YouTube yet, like Florida real estate or Arkansas farm news.
Then I stop talking about it and build one live. I pick tennis, a niche I know nothing about, track a few players in Vid Ninjas, find a breaking umpire controversy, and go from niche to title to script to a fully rendered video with visuals in about 15 minutes. That's not the finished product though. Quality control, editing the script so it actually sounds like you, and fixing the voiceover is what separates a real channel from a lazy one.
I'm Romayroh. I've been doing faceless YouTube since 2018, hundreds of millions of views, and over $2 million in YouTube ad revenue. This is not a guarantee. It took years and it wasn't easy.

Pirates of the Caribbean is considered one of the most immersive attractions ever created for a theme park.

When Walt Disney originally designed the attraction in the 1950s, he imagined it as a wax museum and a walk-through adventure. However, after the success of Walt Disney’s Carousel of Progress at the 1964 New York World’s Fair, Disney and his team of Imagineers decided that Audio-Animatronics—Walt’s latest animation technology—was the most imaginative way to tell a rousing pirate story.

On March 18, 1967, Pirates of the Caribbean opened at Disneyland Park. Thanks to the highly detailed scenes, lavish special effects and memorable characters, the attraction earned rave reviews and has remained a beloved classic ever since.

videos.description:
Khanh’s Moonlit Journey | Ghibli-Inspired Visual Animation & Relaxing Ambient Sounds for Sleep and Study

Khanh’s Moonlit Journey is a peaceful visual animation inspired by the Vietnamese legend of Chú Cuội and the magical banyan tree on the moon.


The animated scenes and ambient sound effects were individually designed and arranged to create a continuous relaxing journey rather than a repeated static loop. This video is suitable for sleep, meditation, studying, reading, stress relief, and quiet background viewing.


According to Vietnamese folklore, Chú Cuội was carried into the sky while holding onto the roots of a magical banyan tree. The tree rose beyond the clouds and reached the moon, where Chú Cuội remained beneath its ancient branches, looking down upon the peaceful villages of Earth.

In this visual adaptation, Khanh follows the banyan tree through the forest, above the clouds, and into the quiet silver landscape of the moon.

🌸 गाँव के मेले की रंगीन शाम | A Beautiful Peaceful Village Life | Ghibli-Inspired Animation 🌿

कभी-कभी जिंदगी की सबसे खूबसूरत खुशियाँ छोटी-छोटी बातों में छिपी होती हैं। ❤️

एक प्यारे से भारतीय गाँव में शुरू होती है माधव और गौरी की खूबसूरत कहानी। सुबह की सुनहरी धूप, चिड़ियों की मीठी चहचहाहट और गाँव की ताजी हवा के बीच गौरी अपने पति माधव के लिए प्यार से नाश्ता तैयार करती है। नाश्ता करने के बाद माधव अपनी पुरानी साइकिल लेकर मिठाई की दुकान पर काम करने निकल जाता है।

दिन धीरे-धीरे गुजरता है और शाम होते ही पूरा गाँव रंग-बिरंगी रोशनियों से जगमगा उठता है। गाँव में मेला लगा है! खूबसूरत सजावट, रंग-बिरंगे खिलौने, पारंपरिक दुकानें और चारों तरफ खुशियों से भरा माहौल। माधव और गौरी मेले में मिलते हैं और साथ मिलकर इस खूबसूरत शाम का आनंद लेते हैं।

दोनों रंगीन खिलौने देखते हैं, मेले की रौनक का आनंद लेते हैं और कुछ प्यारी यादें अपने साथ लेकर घर लौट आते हैं। आखिर में रात के शांत वातावरण में दोनों अपने छोटे से प्यारे घर में आराम से सो जाते हैं।

🌙 यह वीडियो आपको भारतीय गाँव की सादगी, पति-पत्नी के खूबसूरत साथ, बचपन जैसी खुशियों और शांत ग्रामीण जीवन की याद दिलाएगी।

🎨 Video Experience:
• Beautiful original hand-painted 2D animation.
• Peaceful Indian village atmosphere.
• Beautiful morning and sunset scenery.
• Colorful traditional village fair.
• Lovely countryside environment.
• Relaxing natural ASMR sounds.
• Heartwarming husband-wife moments.
• A beautiful and peaceful nighttime ending.

अगर आपको गाँव की जिंदगी, प्रकृति की खूबसूरती और सुकून से भरी ऐसी कहानियाँ पसंद हैं, तो इस वीडियो को अंत तक जरूर देखें। ❤️

videos.description:
लक्ष्मी मैया हमारे घर आना | Lakshmi Maiya Hamare Ghar Aana | Diwali Special Laxmi Ganesh Bhajan

लक्ष्मी मैया हमारे घर आना | Lakshmi Maiya Hamare Ghar Aana | Riddhi Siddhi Sang Bappa Ko Lana | Diwali Special Laxmi Ganesh Bhajan 2026 | ShivRaga Studio

Lakshmi Maiya Hamare Ghar Aana (Riddhi Siddhi Sang Bappa Ko Lana) – Auspicious & Melodious Diwali Special Laxmi-Ganesh Bhajan 2026, by ShivRaga Studio.

लक्ष्मी मैया हमारे घर आना, रिद्धि सिद्धि संग बप्पा को लाना – सुख समृद्धि का दीप जलाना, माँ कृपा का खजाना लुटाना! शुभ दीपावली 🪔🌸🙏

🙏 भजन के बारे में | ABOUT THIS BHAJAN

दीपावली का पर्व अंधकार पर प्रकाश और घर-आंगन में सुख, समृद्धि व शुभता के आगमन का उत्सव है। "लक्ष्मी मैया हमारे घर आना" एक अत्यंत मधुर और मंगलकारी भजन है, जिसमें भक्त अपने द्वार पर तोरण सजाकर, आंगन में घी के दीपक जलाकर माता लक्ष्मी और विघ्नहर्ता श्री गणेश जी (रिद्धि-सिद्धि सहित) को अपने घर पधारने का भावपूर्ण निमंत्रण देता है।

धनतेरस, रूप चौदस, दीपावली की लक्ष्मी-गणेश पूजा, या प्रतिदिन सुबह-शाम की पूजा में इस पावन भजन को अपने घर व दुकान में चलाएं। माता लक्ष्मी आपके घर अन्न-धन के भंडार भरें! जय माँ लक्ष्मी, जय श्री गणेश 🙏✨

"Lakshmi Maiya Hamare Ghar Aana" by ShivRaga Studio is a joyful, festive Hindi devotional bhajan dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Ganesha. With uplifting dholak beats, soothing flute, and the celebratory chorus "Aayi Diwali ki bhor, chhayi khushiyan charon oar", it is the perfect soundtrack for Diwali Puja, Dhanteras, and welcoming prosperity into your home.
